references.text: Jesus urged the disciples to always pray and not lose heart, reflecting the exhortation in Luke 21:36 to pray at all times ([ref:Luk 18:1|Luke 18:1]).
Jesus' parallel warning to stay awake because no one knows the time corresponds to the call to be watchful in Luke 21:36 ([ref:Mark 13:33|Mark 13:33]).
In Gethsemane, Jesus said: "Watch and pray, so that you will not fall into temptation." This same connection between watching and praying appears in Luke 21:36 ([ref:Mark 14:38|Mark 14:38]).
Paul urges believers to pray at all times in the Spirit and to be watchful, which directly parallels Jesus' words about staying awake and praying at all times ([ref:Ef 6:18|Ephesians 6:18]).
Paul's exhortation not to sleep like others but to stay awake and be sober reflects Jesus' call to vigilance in anticipation of the events of the last days ([ref:1 Tess 5:6|1 Thessalonians 5:6]).
Peter writes that the end of all things is near and urges people to be clear-minded and sober so they can pray—an exhortation with the same structure as Luke 21:36 ([ref:1 Pet 4:7|1 Peter 4:7]).

The immediate context warns against letting one's heart be weighed down by drunkenness and daily worries, so that the day comes unexpectedly. The watchfulness in verse 36 is the response to this warning ([ref:Luk 21:34-35|Luke 21:34-35]).
Paul speaks of being counted worthy of God's kingdom, which parallels the desire to be able to stand before the Son of Man ([ref:2 Tess 1:5|2 Thessalonians 1:5]).
The promise of being kept from the hour of trial that will come upon the whole world corresponds to the prayer to escape all that is about to happen ([ref:Åp 3:10|Revelation 3:10]).
The coming of the Son of Man in clouds with power and glory is the event believers must face; verse 36 speaks of being ready for this moment ([ref:Luk 21:27-28|Luke 21:27-28]).

Jude's closing doxology praises Him who is able to keep you from falling and present you faultless before His glory, reflecting the hope of being able to stand before the Son of Man ([ref:Jud 1:24|Jude 1:24]).

Paul urges believers to persevere in prayer and to stay awake in prayer with thanksgiving—an exhortation that aligns with Jesus' words about staying awake and praying at all times ([ref:Kol 4:2|Colossians 4:2]).
